newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seeks to limit duty-free shops in Clark.
newsitem.headline: Manila seeks to limit duty-free shops in Clark.

text.p: The Philippines' Bureau of Customs is seeking to limit the number of duty-free shops operating inside the Clark free port zone, a report released on Tuesday said.

Customs commissioner Guillermo Parayno said a recent investigation found several commercial establishments outside the zone selling imported goods supplied by the duty-free shops but not paying the proper taxes.

Parayno blamed the problem on the proliferation of duty free shops inside Clark, saying some shops have been forced to sell their goods to commercial stores instead of to their target market of foreign travellers and returning overseas Filipino workers.

The report recommended that the government limit the number of duty free stores inside the zone, which currently has more than 10 such stores. The report did not suggest a ceiling figure for the stores.

"It is the firm position of the Bureau that the intense competition brought about by the profliferation of duty free shops at Clark Special Economic Zone is one of the main reasons for the increasing tendency of duty free shops to violate the rules and regulations governing their operations," the report said.
